chunks: 35 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Ibrahim, Sa'dan ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'id, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Malik, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qatawani all narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob al-Zarrad narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Death and killing will encompass people until they resort to the Sanctuary (Kaaba) at that time. Then a truthful caller will cry out due to the intensity of the fighting: 'For what reason is there fighting and killing? Your leader is so-and-so.'

key_terms.الْحَرَم: The Sanctuary (specifically the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.مُنَادٍ صَادِق: A truthful caller (often interpreted as an angel or divine voice)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say about the signs of fighting and the arrival of the Mahdi?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the 'Satanic' nature of the pre-Mahdi civil strife, where the conflict itself becomes the primary motivator for people to seek refuge in the Haram. The 'truthful caller' (Munadi) serves as a divine sign, clarifying that the prolonged bloodshed is not random but is directly linked to the emergence of the Mahdi, who is identified as the root cause of this turmoil. This event underscores the transition from chaotic persecution to the establishment of justice, a theme central to Shia eschatology.
